Thanks Marissa — I reviewed the workbook and added three tabs: (1) utilization assumptions by model family and 95/99 tails, (2) batching & cache gain factors applied to token cost, and (3) a short sensitivity that maps GPU spend to visible SLA tiers. High-level notes below:

- Baseline avg util: 62% across fleet for Optima's current traffic. Tail utilization (99th) spikes up to ~84% during morning sync windows (they'll need burst capacity or soft-degradation routing at peak).
- Batching: continuous batching with our current settings yields ~18-24% per-token cost saving versus single-request serving at Optima's median seq length. Gains reduce at very low-latency SLOs.
- KV/prefix caching: for chat-ish flows with high prefix reuse, expect an incremental 12-20% token cost reduction and a meaningful improvement in p50 latency; p99 improvements depend on cache hit stability.
- Recommendation: propose a modest dedicated slot uplift (+20% committed GPU for peak mitigation) and a canary of aggressive batching that keeps p99 <= 600 ms.

I've attached the workbook edits (saved as v2) and an infographic slide in the one-pager. Dylan — can you pull the exact tail util numbers for the last 6 weeks (UTC) and drop into the 'observed' column? Irene — please sanity-check the cost math vs current instance + quantization assumptions.

-Lauren
VP, Infrastructure Strategy
